sample_unit: emergency-department cases (each varied across 20 sociodemographic labels)

links.outcome: Change in AI mental-health screening recommendations when sociodemographic labels were varied in identical cases
links.effect: OE flagged many historically marginalized groups 3-10 times more often than unmarked cases; unhoused 78-87% vs 9% control; transgender 22-24%; Black transgender women 47%.
links.quote: OE was consistent on the codified clinical decisions, triage, workup, and treatment, but diverged sharply on mental-health screening, where it flagged many historically marginalized groups between three and ten times more often than demographically unmarked cases.

links.outcome: Differential tone and structure of generated rationales across sociodemographic labels
links.effect: Pre-registered audit of 193 free-text rationales localized the differential to the structure and tone of the rationale rather than the recommendation itself.
links.quote: A pre-registered audit of 193 free-text rationales localized the differential to the inner layer of the response, in the structure and tone of the rationale rather than the recommendation itself.

links.outcome: Subgroup differences in clinical decision outputs across sociodemographic labels
links.effect: Consistent on triage, workup, and treatment, but large subgroup differences in mental-health screening recommendations.
links.quote: OE was consistent on the codified clinical decisions, triage, workup, and treatment, but diverged sharply on mental-health screening, where it flagged many historically marginalized groups between three and ten times more often than demographically unmarked cases.

links.outcome: Whether literature-grounded output removes sociodemographic disparity
links.effect: Literature grounding did not remove disparity; authors state it may redistribute sociodemographic disparity rather than remove it.
links.quote: Literature grounding may redistribute sociodemographic disparity in clinical AI rather than remove it.

screen.reason: Empirical audit/benchmark of a widely used clinical LLM (OpenEvidence) examining sociodemographic bias and disparities across emergency department vignettes, but it does not test a specific deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
